macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks plunge as chip sector sells off
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.2% and the S&P 500 dropped 1.9%, while the Dow declined 0.9% during Thursday trading. Chip stocks led the retreat amid concerns about tighter scrutiny of artificial-intelligence infrastructure following the Democratic midterm-election victory.[1]

items.title: AI and semiconductor shares drive broader market volatility
items.summary: Qualcomm, Micron and Arm Holdings led declines across the chip sector; Arm fell nearly 11% after its guidance failed to exceed expectations, while Qualcomm dropped more than 9% on weaker smartphone-chip revenue and higher supply-chain costs.[1]

items.title: Oil prices fall sharply after U.S. election result
items.summary: Brent crude fell nearly 9% and moved below $100 a barrel as investors assessed the prospect of an end to the U.S.-Iran conflict. Lower energy prices supported bonds and pushed U.S. Treasury yields lower.[1]

items.title: Fed officials emphasize inflation risks
items.summary: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said inflation remains the Federal Reserve’s most important risk and that the AI buildout has increased demand. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack also warned that inflation pressures could spread while the labor market strengthens.[1]

items.title: U.S. labor and productivity data remain resilient
items.summary: Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 for the week ended October 31, matching the lowest level since 1969. Third-quarter productivity grew 3.6%, while unit labor costs declined 0.7%, strengthening the case for continued attention to inflation and monetary policy.[1]

items.title: Markets price a possible December Fed rate hike
items.summary: Futures markets assigned roughly an 80% probability to a Federal Reserve rate increase at the December 9 meeting, after the Fed held its policy rate at 3.75%–4.00% on October 28.[1]

items.title: U.S. payrolls report becomes the next major market catalyst
items.summary: Investors are awaiting October employment data, with forecasts for 65,000 payroll additions, unemployment of 4.2%, and monthly wage growth of 0.3%. The report is expected to influence expectations for the Fed’s December decision.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rises above $80,000 as crypto market rebounds
items.summary: Bitcoin gained roughly 4.8% in 24 hours to about $80,721, while the broader crypto market rose approximately 4.7% to $2.69 trillion. The move was amplified by nearly $1 billion in liquidations, including more than $386 million in short positions.[1]

items.title: Bitcoin and Ether rally as ETF inflows return
items.summary: Bitcoin moved above $80,000 and Ether gained nearly 6% as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $74.6 million in net inflows, ending a three-day withdrawal streak.[3]

items.title: U.S. regulators advance stablecoin and tokenization rules
items.summary: The Federal Reserve proposed prudential standards for stablecoin issuers under the Genius Act. Separately, the CFTC updated guidance allowing registrants to invest customer funds in eligible tokenized assets and use blockchain systems for recordkeeping.[10]

items.title: SEC issues no-action positions for DoubleZero and Canton Coin
items.summary: The SEC’s corporate-finance division issued a no-action letter for DoubleZero’s 2Z token and reportedly declined enforcement over Canton Coin’s programmatic minting, describing it as a digital commodity rather than a security.[2][3]

items.title: Schroders launches tokenized debt fund on Solana
items.summary: Asset manager Schroders launched a tokenized emerging-markets debt fund through Centrifuge on Solana, marking its first deployment on the blockchain.[3]

items.title: World Liberty Financial brings USD1 stablecoin to Aptos
items.summary: World Liberty Financial announced that its dollar-pegged USD1 stablecoin will launch on Aptos, its first deployment on a Move-based blockchain.[2]

items.title: South Korea considers another crypto-tax delay
items.summary: South Korea’s Democratic Party formally proposed postponing the country’s 22% cryptocurrency income tax, which would represent the fourth delay since 2020.[3]

items.title: France advances disclosure requirement for large self-hosted wallets
items.summary: France’s National Assembly adopted an amendment requiring declarations for self-hosted crypto wallets valued at €100,000 or more, with potential fines of up to €10,000 for noncompliance.[3]

items.title: Fitell buys $1.5 million of Pump.fun tokens
items.summary: Australia-based Fitell Corporation announced the purchase of 216.8 million PUMP tokens for $1.5 million as it expands its Solana-focused digital-asset treasury strategy.[2]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic AI development reportedly accelerating
items.summary: An independent METR analysis says Anthropic’s AI systems are improving about twice as quickly as a year ago, despite CEO Dario Amodei’s calls to slow capability growth. The report also says Anthropic has trained three unreleased models in the past six months.

items.title: UK warns of AI-enabled attacks on critical infrastructure
items.summary: Britain’s cyber chief warned that AI-powered attacks against critical infrastructure are likely by 2028, potentially involving ransomware and other malware deployed by criminal groups or states.

items.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-Image-2.6
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly rolling out GPT-Image-2.6 in ChatGPT and Codex, with faster image generation, GIF creation, frame-level editing, and API availability for new variants.

items.title: Nanbeige releases open-weights 33B reasoning model
items.summary: Nanbeige released a 33-billion-parameter open-weights reasoning model that reportedly matches Qwen3.8 27B on one cited evaluation and performs substantially better on Terminal-Bench, though with higher token usage.

items.title: Google makes Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available
items.summary: Google DeepMind reportedly made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available, adding 15-second video generation and multi-turn editing while reducing the listed price from the previous version.

items.title: Baidu introduces AI simulation system for robotaxis
items.summary: Baidu launched Apollo World, a system designed to simulate up to 100,000 kilometers of driving daily using multimodal camera and lidar data for autonomous-vehicle development and testing.

items.title: Enterprise AI agents remain limited in autonomous decision-making
items.summary: A TCS study reported that only about 10% of global enterprises currently allow AI agents to make decisions autonomously, reflecting continued concerns about safeguards, governance, and reliability.

items.title: Google tests AI processing aboard satellite
items.summary: Google’s Project Suncatcher reportedly completed early machine-learning tests using an onboard Gemma model, marking an early demonstration of running AI workloads in space.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Steam tightens game-submission requirements amid AI-generated content surge
items.summary: Valve is requiring developers to run submitted games for at least five minutes and verify redistributables, achievements, and cloud features. The changes follow a sharp rise in store-page and build-review submissions, which has contributed to release delays.

items.title: Arkane Lyon union opposes potential studio closure
items.summary: The French game-workers union STJV says closing Arkane Lyon could cost Microsoft more than completing Marvel’s Blade. The union says 217 employees are affected and reports that Ubisoft may be interested in acquiring the studio.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI hype intensifies ahead of launch
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is being described as potentially the biggest video-game release ever, with players, streamers, and professional athletes discussing its expected cultural impact. The game is scheduled for release on November 19, 2026.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls VI reportedly remains more than two years away
items.summary: Reports following Bethesda’s recent reveal of the game’s title, Sentinel, suggest the long-awaited RPG may still be over two years from release, prompting renewed frustration among fans.

items.title: PlayStation updates Assassin’s Creed Valhalla for PS5 Pro
items.summary: A new update adds New Game+ and improved PSSR support for PlayStation 5 Pro players.
